Montauk
Pink Lemonade
FMB
ABV5.0%
Sugar0g
Cal100

This seltzer is great. Slightly sweet, but not overbearing in it's sweetness. A hint of lemon with a hint of pink. No artificial flavor. Zero aftertaste. A great combination of sweetness, flavor, and drinkability. Love the look of the can. RE REVIEW 07/05/2026: We're back at the greatest seltzer of all time! The number 1 seltzer from many moons ago may just be the #1 today. Though i'm not in a position at the moment to change the ranking of this seltzer, it was due time for a REAL review. After consuming over 500 seltzers, i can safely say that this still, in the year of our lord 2026, is a GREAT DRINK. At first i was very surprised that this drink really holds up to this day, but was confused as to why. When you crack into this can, you are hit with a delicious lemony taste that borders on the sour pink side. Though there is no sugar added to this drink, it's not sweetened by too much artificial sweetener, and i believe it gets it's taste from the minimal amount of Juice added. IT HAS THE JUICE! 4%, apparently. If pink lemonade was an actual natural flavor that existed in the real world, this would be the perfect embodiment of it. This is totally drinkable, and it's sourness wouldn't overburden you after 8-10 of these. It would leave you wanting more. I'm happy to say that this drink holds up, but i'm not in a position yet to dethrone the drink until we do an upcoming blind taste test. More to come, but drink this seltzer.

Montauk
Original Lemonade
FMB

Natural lemonade, no artificial flavor. More tart than sweet, not overbearing on the tartness but noticeable. Maybe the best lemonade seltzer on the market. Could be higher if not for the Pink Lemonade flavor being just slightly more palatable. RE REVIEW 07/28/2026: This happens to be the first seltzer i've had in 3 weeks, and i'm happy to report that it's an excellent choice! After re-reading my comments from over 2 years ago, it's safe to say that the review holds up. This seltzer is an excellent representation of Lemonade style seltzers. Much better than your traditional Mike's lemonades, or even some fruity lemon bastardizations, this is a very natural tasting lemon with a hint of ade. Just like i mentioned 2 years ago, this strikes the perfect mix between sweet and tart, creating a very pleasant flavor that is sustainable over time. You can safely drink a bushel full of these seltzers without getting tired of the taste. Montauk has done something special with these seltzers, and i'm glad to see that it has held up for over 2 years and 500+ seltzers. If you can find a pack of these Montauks somewhere, do yourself a favor and pick them up. Probably the best thing to come out of Long Island since the iced tea.

THE BIG 500!!! This is the 500th seltzer to grace this list, and i'm happy to report that it is a fantastic drink! It would have been so dissapointing if #500 was terrible, but the good people at sandbagger have done it again! They've consistently created top tier seltzers, and this is the first i've had in their vodka foray. I'm told that the word "cranfusion" is new to the lexicon, and in the same vein as edgar allen poe creating the word "tintinnabulation", sandbagger is bringing a banger of a word into our collective zeitgeist alsong with a banger of a drink. The flavor is a great mix of cranberry and ginger, and this somehow hits the perfect middle ground for a ranberry seltzer: it's not too tart, and not too sweet, which means you can drink many of these and still want more. I believe the natural tartness of the cranberry is somehow offset by the sweetness of the ginger, and of course the vodka flavor is non-existent, which is exactly where you want it to be. I'm excited to try the other vodkas in sandbagger's collection, and i hope you are too.

Then add the floral taste of hibiscus, which is all the rage in seltzers, and you've got the combination from apple hell. My recommendation is if you see this seltzer on the menu, avoid it at all costs.
